draft.title: Aphantasia
card: Aphantasia is the inability to form mental images. A person with it cannot picture a scene, face or object in their mind's eye.
It is not a loss of memory. People with aphantasia can still learn, store and recall facts, such as the capital of France or how to ride a bike.
Many people with aphantasia recall past personal events with less detail. They may know what happened but cannot replay it as a picture.
Recalling an event often draws on visual detail, so having no mental pictures can leave the memory thinner.
draft.remember: Aphantasia removes mental pictures, not memory itself. Facts stay, but event memories are often less detailed.

a.q: Which description best fits a person with aphantasia?
opts: Cannot picture images, but can still recall facts
Cannot store new facts, but can picture images
Cannot recall facts or picture images in the mind
Pictures images clearly but cannot recall events
a.why: Aphantasia is about mental imagery, not memory storage, so facts can still be recalled. The tempting option about losing facts and pictures treats it as general memory loss, which it is not.
a.clue: Aphantasia affects the mind's eye, not the ability to learn facts.

b.q: Leila has aphantasia. She is asked about her last birthday party and about the rules of netball. Which result is most likely?
opts: She gives few vivid party details but states the rules
She states the rules poorly but gives vivid party details
She recalls both with little detail because memory is weaker
She cannot recall that the party happened at all
b.why: Netball rules are facts, which people with aphantasia can still recall. The party is a personal event, which is often recalled with less detail without mental images. The option claiming weaker memory overall is tempting but treats aphantasia as general memory loss.
b.clue: Separate memory for facts from memory for personal events.

a.best: Cannot picture images, but can still recall facts

b.best: She gives few vivid party details but states the rules

problems.detail: The card gives 'how to ride a bike' as an example of a fact. Riding a bike is procedural (implicit) memory, not a fact (semantic, explicit memory). VCE Psychology students must keep these memory types apart, so this example could mislead them. Use a factual example instead, such as a date or a definition.
